edges.description: Failure of haematopoietic precursor survival removes the progenitors from which thymocytes would derive.
The same precursor-survival defect abolishes granulocyte production, a myeloid consequence absent from the other SCID subtypes.
Absent haematopoietic precursors leave the primary and secondary lymphoid organs hypoplastic.
Absence of functional T lymphocytes abolishes cell-mediated immunity and (directly or via loss of T-cell help) humoral immunity.
Blocked thymic T-cell development produces profound T lymphocytopenia.
Absence of developing thymocytes leaves a small, dysplastic thymus that yields an absent thymic shadow on imaging.
In T-B- subtypes (RAG1/RAG2, Artemis, ADA) the same developmental/metabolic block also abolishes B-lymphocyte development.

evidence.snippet: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency is a systemic purine metabolic disorder that primarily affects lymphocyte development, viability, and function.

The ADA deficiency phenotypic spectrum includes typical early-onset severe combined immunodeficiency (ADA-SCID), diagnosed in infancy (about 80% of individuals), and less severe "delayed" or "late-onset" combined immunodeficiency (ADA-CID), diagnosed in older children and adults (15%-20% of individuals).
Mutation of the AK2 gene causes reticular dysgenesis (RD), an autosomal recessive disorder occurring in 2% of children with SCID.
Deficiency of AK2 is associated with lack of innate and adaptive immunity.
Adenylate kinases are involved in cellular and mitochondrial energy homeostasis.

nodes.description: Absent granulocytes with profound neutropenia is the feature that separates reticular dysgenesis from every other SCID subtype, and follows from the haematopoietic-precursor rather than lymphoid-specific block.

nodes.description: In X-linked SCID, JAK3 deficiency, and IL7R deficiency, loss-of-function in the common gamma chain (IL2RG), its associated kinase JAK3, or the IL-7 receptor alpha chain abolishes IL-7-dependent JAK-STAT signaling that drives early thymocyte survival and proliferation, blocking T-cell development. IL2RG and JAK3 defects additionally abrogate NK-cell development (T-B+NK-), whereas IL7R defects spare B and NK cells (T-B+NK+).

evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of typical and atypical X-SCID is established in a male proband with suggestive findings and a hemizygous pathogenic variant in IL2RG identified by molecular genetic testing.

The encoded protein is expressed on the lymphoid lineage and is required during T cell development during early stage and for proliferation and survival of T cells in the periphery.

nodes.description: In RAG1, RAG2, and DCLRE1C (Artemis) deficiency, the machinery that assembles antigen-receptor genes is impaired. RAG1/RAG2 initiate site-specific DNA cleavage during V(D)J recombination, and Artemis opens the resulting DNA hairpins as part of non-homologous end-joining. Failure to recombine T-cell (and B-cell) receptor genes arrests lymphocyte development (T-B-NK+); Artemis loss additionally confers cellular radiosensitivity.

evidence.snippet: RAG1 and RAG2, are DNA recombinases that mediate DNA recombination process and ensure the somatic diversification of immunoglobulin and TCR genes during B-cell and T-cell development, respectively.
In the absence of VDJ recombination, T cell undergoes apoptosis.

DCLRE1C encodes ARTEMIS, a nuclease which is single-stranded with- 5′-3′ exonuclease potential and endonuclease activity over 5′ and 3′ ends. It is essential for V(D)J rearrangement and for DNA repair.
Patients with this form of SCID are sensitive to ionizing radiation and chemotherapeutic agents.

nodes.description: In reticular dysgenesis, loss of adenylate kinase 2 disrupts cellular and mitochondrial energy homeostasis in haematopoietic precursors themselves. Because the lesion is bioenergetic rather than lymphoid-specific, both myeloid and lymphoid output fail: granulocytes are absent alongside lymphocytes, and innate as well as adaptive immunity is lost. This is the one SCID mechanism class in this entry whose consequences extend outside the lymphoid lineage.

nodes.description: For ADA deficiency, enzyme replacement therapy with PEGylated adenosine deaminase corrects the metabolic defect, providing protection against infection; it is often used to stabilize patients before curative HSCT or gene therapy.

evidence.snippet: enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) by intramuscular administration of PEGylated ADA

Often, ERT is initiated first to rapidly correct the metabolic defect and to protect against serious infections as well as neurologic/behavioral abnormalities. It is discontinued at the time HSCT or HSC-GT is performed.

nodes.description: Until immune reconstitution is achieved, exposure avoidance is itself treatment. Live viral vaccines — given to the infant or to household contacts — can cause disseminated vaccine-strain disease; non-irradiated blood products can cause transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease in a patient with no T cells to reject donor lymphocytes; and breast milk is withheld pending maternal CMV status. Live rotavirus vaccine is the specific exposure that newborn-screening programmes act on first, because it is administered at the age at which screened infants are still awaiting definitive therapy.
